resources.string: I’m wysie, and this is my personal edition of Zeekr Shortcut. I maintain it primarily for my ZEEKR 009, with my own improvements, experiments and contributions adapted from the open-source community.
My source code and downloads are linked below, alongside dts88’s original project. For issues with wysie Edition, please use my repository and attach a report from Settings → System → Diagnostics.

Recordings go to USB drives only, not to the head unit's internal storage (except with developer options): its write endurance is limited and it can't be replaced.

• The USB drive supplied with the car is enough for basic recording.

• For higher bitrates or longer retention without using the car's own drive, add a USB drive or SSD to the left Type-C port. It is detected automatically and can be removed at any time.

• With Sentry Mode on after you leave the car, only the USB-A port stays powered. A drive on the Type-C port loses power, and recording moves to the drive on the USB-A port.

• Tested: a 128 GB USB drive, and an NVMe SSD (much faster, runs slightly warmer).

• Optane M10 drives are good value but small: about the last 20 hours of recordings, depending on capacity and bitrate.

Recordings and photos stay on your USB drive. The app does not upload them.

⚠ Recordings and photos on the drive are not encrypted. Anyone with the drive can read them.

The app goes online only when you start one of these:

• Check for updates: asks GitHub for the latest version and, if you confirm, downloads it from GitHub. No device data is sent.

• Send to phone: serves one file on your local network until you close the window.
Experimental, unofficial software, not affiliated with ZEEKR. While driving, watch the road, not this app. Recordings are not guaranteed to be complete. Use at your own risk.
